NEW YORK WORLD-TELEGRAM & SUN
New York, New York
December 6, 1954

Dr. Hockett Joins
Tobacco Group
Dr. Robert C. Hockett has
been named an associate scien-
tific director of the Tobacco
Industry
Research Com-
mittee, it was
announced
today by Dr.
Clarence Cook
Little, scientific
director.
Dr. Hockett
will aid Dr.
Little and the
Scientific Dr. R. C. Hockett
Advisory Board in developing
the tobacco industry’s program
of research into tobacco use and
health, it was said. The com-
mittee recently made initial
grants of $82,000 to six institu-
tions for basic research projects
and is reviewing applications
for additional grants. Dr. Hock-
ett spent nine years prior to
1952 as scientific director of the
Sugar Research Foundation.

NEW YORK TIMES
New York, New York
December 6, 1954

Tobacco Research Aide Named
WASHINGTON, Dec. 5 (UP)—
Dr. Robert C. Hockett was ap-
pointed today associate scientific
director of the Tobacco Industry
Research Committee. Dr. Hock-
ett, a native of Fayette, Mo., will
assist the committee in research
in tobacco use and health. Dr.
Hockett until recently was a
consultant to Arthur D. Little,
Inc., and to pharmaceutical, food
and beverage companies. He is a
former associate professor of
chemistry at the Massachusetts
Institute of Technology.

WALL STREET JOURNAL
New York, New York
December 7, 1954

Tobacco Industry to Back Study
NEW YORK—The tobacco industry’s re-
search committee expects to spend about $60,-
000 in the first year on a new project it's
launching to study human lung ailments.
The committee plans to give a research
grant to a group of pathologists to conduct
examinations of the bronchial system and the
lungs. The data collected will be gathered at
a central location for tabulating, comparing
and analyzing. The group met here to discuss
and plan the program, and will adopt specific
plans at a later meeting.

COR TI 14671
